Choice.value: In-scope: current space containing the camera
OOS: open or ambiguous boundary of the current space

Text.name: scope_rule_text
Text.value: Annotate the current space containing the camera. Follow its enclosing walls through corners that belong to the current space. When an opening leads to an adjacent space, close at a clear structural boundary such as a door frame, paired wall returns or jambs, or an arch. Local occlusion, openings, stairs, or ceiling recesses are not automatically OOS. Scope remains the authoritative OOS field.

Choice.hint: Choose only when no other factor materially increases layout or corner annotation difficulty. This label is mutually exclusive with every other difficulty label.
A foreground object or structure blocks wall, corner, or boundary evidence that would otherwise need to be judged.
The image is complete, but local texture, color, or contrast is too weak to locate structural boundaries reliably.
Panorama stitching, reprojection, or stretching breaks or shifts lines, bends walls, or displaces corners.
Mirrors or glass create false boundaries, duplicated structure, or depth confusion that materially increases annotation difficulty.

Choice.value: Blur, mask, or low image quality
Choice.hint: Blur, noise, compression, masks, black borders, or missing pixels make key structural evidence unreliable.

Text.name: difficulty_rule_text
Text.value: Select the factors that materially made layout or corner annotation harder in this task. Difficulty does not determine Scope or indicate whether the model is wrong. Select distinct independent factors, but do not apply multiple labels to the same underlying cause. Trivial is mutually exclusive with all concrete factors.

Choice.hint: The initial model geometry needs no adjustment and can be submitted unchanged. This label is mutually exclusive with every concrete issue.
The model crosses a clear structural boundary and includes an adjacent space.
The model misses walls, corners, or boundaries that belong to the current space.
The model treats non-layout details as real structure.
A corner or local-boundary position needs adjustment while the point count and topology are otherwise correct.
Multiple redundant points represent the same physical corner.
Corner correspondence, order, closure, or another structural configuration is invalid.
Choose only when the initial prediction is missing, unusable, or cannot be adequately described by a concrete issue. Do not additionally select fail when concrete issues already describe the error.

Text.name: model_issue_rule_text
Text.value: Judge the initial model proposal before editing. Acceptable means the initial geometry needs no adjustment and can be submitted unchanged; it is mutually exclusive with every concrete issue. If any corner, boundary, or topology needs correction, choose the corresponding issue. Never replace the worker's explicit answer with a geometry-based inference.
